h1: The 4 Best Battery Backpack Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Backpack Leaf Blowers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four battery backpack leaf blowers from WORX and Greenworks, compared on airflow, voltage and who each one suits.
summary: The WORX backpack blower is the safe default for a large yard, though its listing gives no airflow figure. The Greenworks 40V lists the most airflow at 660 CFM, and the Greenworks 60V suits owners of other 60V tools. The Greenworks Pro adds a stated 150 MPH for stubborn debris.
intro: Shopping a battery backpack blower on airflow alone is how people end up with a machine that hangs badly, tires the shoulders and gets retired after ten minutes. The harness decides whether the blower gets used for a full cleanup. The battery platform decides whether the next tool you buy costs a little or a lot. The headline cubic feet per minute is only the starting point.

We reviewed the backpack models in this price band and ranked them on spec sheets and the detail each listing gives. Four true backpack designs made the cut, all from WORX and Greenworks, and every one sits in the $200 to $500 bucket. Handheld blowers were left out because they are a different tool with a different job. Listings that publish more numbers scored better.

products.name: WORX Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The safe default for a yard that is too big for a handheld.
products.description:
The WORX backpack blower is a battery-powered backpack design from a well-known brand, priced in the $200 to $500 bucket. A backpack shifts the weight from one arm to the shoulders and hips, which is why larger yards need one and why handhelds tire people out. Battery power also means no cord and no fuel to carry.

It ranks first because the brand and the straightforward backpack format are the safest purchase here, and its price matches the rest. But it publishes no CFM figure, which keeps it from a higher score on information.

Buy it for a larger yard if you want a backpack blower without fuss. The caveat is a thin spec sheet, so skip it if you want a published airflow number before buying. Confirm the specifications on the product page before ordering.
products.idealFor: Homeowners with a larger yard who want a backpack blower without fuss.
products.skipIf: You want a published airflow number before buying.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The highest listed airflow of the four backpack picks.
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V backpack blower lists 660 CFM of airflow, in a cordless backpack design. Volume of air is what clears wide piles quickly, and 660 CFM is the highest figure among the four. The 40V platform also suits owners of other Greenworks 40V tools.

It ranks second because it lists no air speed and runs on a lower voltage than the 60V pair. In pure airflow it beats the 550 CFM models by 110, which is a meaningful gap on a big lawn.

Buy it if you want the most listed airflow in a backpack blower. Skip it if you already own 60V Greenworks batteries, since those will not fit. Compare the battery cost against the saved time before choosing.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the most listed airflow in a backpack blower.

products.name: Greenworks 60V Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 60V backpack blower with a clearly stated 550 CFM.
products.description:
The Greenworks 60V backpack blower states 550 CFM, with cordless operation on the 60V platform. A 60V battery is shared across other 60V tools from the same brand, so owners of a mower or trimmer on that voltage save money.

It ranks third because the listing offers less airflow than the 40V and no weight figure. At 550 CFM, it handles dry leaves and clippings but is less suited to heavy wet piles.

Buy it if you own other 60V Greenworks tools and want to share batteries. Skip it if maximum airflow matters more than voltage. Check what the kit includes, because batteries are the expensive part.
products.skipIf: Maximum airflow matters more than voltage.

products.name: Greenworks Pro 60-Volt Max Lithium Ion 550-CFM 150-MPH Heavy-Duty
products.verdict: A heavy-duty 60V backpack blower with both CFM and MPH in the name.
products.description:
The Greenworks Pro 60V Max heavy-duty backpack blower lists 550 CFM and 150 MPH, with a lithium ion battery. Air speed, as well as volume, matters here: 150 MPH helps lift wet or stuck debris that volume alone leaves behind, and few listings publish it.

It ranks last because its airflow matches the cheaper Greenworks 60V and trails the 40V's 660 CFM. Its advantage is the stated speed.

Buy it if you want both airflow and air speed stated, especially for wet leaves. Skip it if you want the highest CFM in the group. Because the Pro is the only model to list MPH, it gives the clearest picture of its performance.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want both airflow and air speed stated.
products.skipIf: You want the highest CFM in the group.

whatMatters.detail: CFM measures the volume of air the blower moves each minute. A higher figure clears wide piles faster, so it matters on larger lawns. Look for the number in the title or bullet points rather than a vague phrase like powerful airflow. The Greenworks 40V lists 660 CFM and the 60V models 550, while the WORX gives none, which makes comparison harder.

MPH describes how fast the air leaves the nozzle. High speed lifts wet or stuck debris that volume alone leaves behind. Few listings state it, so treat a published MPH figure as a useful extra detail. Only the Greenworks Pro lists one, at 150 MPH, which makes it easier to judge for wet leaves than the others.

Voltage sets which battery platform you are buying into. A 60V blower shares batteries with other 60V tools from the same brand, while a 40V does not. Check what tools you already own before choosing, because batteries are expensive and a second platform means two chargers on the shelf and two sets of batteries to maintain.

A backpack design moves weight from your arm to your shoulders and hips. That matters over long sessions, since a handheld tires the wrist within minutes. Confirm the listing says backpack, because some battery blowers are handheld, and check for harness details, such as padding and straps, if the listing provides any.

Backpack blowers range widely in cost once batteries are included. Compare the price range shown and confirm whether the battery and charger come in the box before you buy. All four here sit in the $200 to $500 bucket, but the cost of an extra battery can add a large amount to the real total.

faq.q: Do these blowers come with a battery?
faq.a: The listings we reviewed do not make this clear. Check the product page for whether the battery and charger are included before you order, because the pack is the expensive part of a cordless kit, and a bare tool can cost as much again.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying?
faq.a: Choosing on CFM alone. Air speed, battery platform and comfort all affect how the blower performs in practice. A strong blower that hangs badly gets used less than a modest one that fits well, so comfort deserves weight.

faq.q: Is a 60V blower worth it over a 40V?
faq.a: Only if you own or plan to buy other 60V tools. On paper the 40V Greenworks lists more airflow than either 60V model here, 660 CFM against 550, so voltage alone does not mean more power, and you should compare the CFM figures directly.

faq.q: How do I check airflow on a listing?
faq.a: Look for a CFM number in the title or bullet points. The WORX listing gives none, so confirm it on the product page or from the maker before you commit to it, since an unlisted figure is a missing fact.

faq.q: How should I care for the battery?
faq.a: Follow the manufacturer's guidance in the manual. Store it as directed and avoid leaving it fully drained for long periods. Keep batteries out of extreme heat or cold between uses, and charge them on a hard surface away from clutter.

faq.q: Can a backpack blower handle wet leaves?
faq.a: Air speed matters most for wet debris. Only the Greenworks Pro lists an MPH figure, at 150 MPH, so it is the clearest choice for wet leaves among the four.

finalTake: The WORX backpack blower is the safe pick for a larger yard if you accept a thin spec sheet. The Greenworks 40V gives the most listed airflow, and the Greenworks Pro is the one that publishes air speed. Check the battery platform and what is in the box before you buy.
